title: Machine learning flagged foodborne outbreaks in national surveillance data
summary: Using China’s Foodborne Disease Monitoring and Reporting System, the study trained models to identify suspected outbreaks. XGBoost achieved recall 0.9699 and F1 0.9582 on a held-out test set and assigned high outbreak probabilities to three confirmed 2019 outbreaks. The known outbreaks were checked retrospectively; prospective surveillance benefit was not tested.
ai_technology: XGBoost and other machine-learning classifiers; SHAP
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: The paper reports a 75/25 train/test split and retrospective checks of three known outbreaks; no external or prospective evaluation is shown.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: Classifiers identify suspected foodborne outbreaks from case, exposure, symptom and diagnosis features; SHAP was used to interpret predictions.

source_review.scope: Read the original full text, including author affiliations, Methods and Results; checked the first result-bearing version and active/archive catalog for same-result records.
